feature_notes:
Adds usable canonical Rust resource controls to Python: ResourceLimits exposes all twenty read/edit limits; SharedStringOptions selects auto/memory/disk SST placement with RAM/cache/temp/entry limits and temp_directory; AutoMemory controls headroom, fraction, maximum, caller availability and anticipated concurrent operations; ResourceOptions also bounds editable patches. load_workbook(resource_options=...) forwards owned immutable settings to Rust. New ordinary/write-only Workbook instances accept auto_memory; model_memory_budget_bytes exposes their selected model allowance. Mode-inapplicable options and invalid types/ranges reject explicitly. Compression remains a per-save option; backend selection is compile-time.

Pins canonical Rust alpha.5 revision 7efa37b10c6b19757ff58dbf930f9e233b3af7d4. Core M2 acceptance is verified with bounded high-cardinality SSTs, complete assigned value/string/date/formula reads, read-side styles, native desktop probes, owned theme catalogs/formula references, concurrency-aware Auto and exact style integer identities. Full Python style/rich/feature proxies and M4-M7 remain staged; core acceptance is not a full adapter compatibility claim.

Temporal replacement tests consolidate forty invocations into two without dropping any combination or save/readback assertion. Three batched resource tests verify actual parser/archive/row/batch/model/edit limits, actual SST spill/cache/temp settings, source protection and cleanup. Original pinned upstream test bodies/licenses are unchanged. Candidate wheels pass all 544 tests on CPython 3.11-3.15; Ruff format/check, Rustfmt and strict Clippy pass.

Publication builds/tests all 25 wheels using five shared-compilation platform jobs (Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows x86_64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon) and tests an independent sdist before PyPI OIDC upload. Core MSRV stays Rust 1.88; wheels use latest stable Rust. Resource allowances are managed limits, not hard whole-process RSS caps; loaded model/reader/editor allowances remain separate. Native desktop host probes do not discover private job/process constraints: use available_bytes or explicit budgets on constrained hosts. concurrent_operations divides anticipated allowances and does not create threads. RAM/disk/concurrency performance tradeoffs and raw evidence are documented in the canonical core. Unsupported APIs raise explicit errors without silent fallback.
